chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with leasing the land from its owner for twenty years, and less than that and more. So he cultivates it and pays whatever taxes are upon it, and he does not include the non-Muslims (Ahl al-Zimma) in anything from the lease, because it is not permissible.

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: The owners or inhabitants of the land.
key_terms.الْعُلُوج: Non-Muslims (specifically Ahl al-Zimma, people of the covenant).
key_terms.قَبَالَة: Leasing or renting of land, specifically agricultural land.
key_terms.يَعْمُرُهَا: He cultivates or works the land.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for leasing land and the ruling on including non-Muslims in the lease according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the duration of agricultural land lease (qabala) is flexible, allowing for twenty years or any other period, provided the lessee cultivates the land and fulfills tax obligations. A key jurisprudential nuance is the prohibition of including 'al-uluj' (often interpreted as non-Muslims or specific tax-paying groups) in the lease, reflecting the distinct legal status of Ahl al-Zimma in Islamic governance. This ruling underscores the practical application of land management principles within the Shia fiqh tradition, emphasizing both economic utility and religious compliance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
from Abu Abdullah(a.s.) having said:

‘There is no problem with leasing the land from its owner for twenty years, and less from that and more. So work on it and pay whatever taxes that are upon it, and do not include the non-Muslims in anything from the lease, because it is not Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is not unlawful to reach an agreement with the owners of the land for twenty years or less or more, then revive it and pay what he spends on it; but one must not include al-‘ilj (the infidels) in the agreement because it is not lawful.’”
